nodes.Preparation: Kanji is prepared by fermenting a mixture of rice (or rice gruel) with water and souring agents (such as mustard or spices) for a specific period until it becomes acidic.

nodes.label: Mundi Kwatha
nodes.Preparation: Decoction prepared from whole plant of Sphaeranthus indicus Linn.

nodes.label: Panchapallava Kwatha
nodes.Preparation: Decoction prepared from leaves of Amra (Mangifera indica), Jambu (Syzygium cumini), Kapittha (Limonia acidissima), Bilwa (Aegle marmelos), Bijapuraka (Citrus medica) boiled in water.

nodes.label: Gandhodaka
nodes.Preparation: Aromatic herbal Decoction prepared by boiling Twakpatri (leaves of Cinnamomum zeylanicum Breyn.), Patraka (leaves of Cinnamomum tamala N.), Ushira (roots of Vetiveria zizanoides L.), Musta (tubers of Cyperus rotundus L.), Balamula (roots of Sida cordifolia L., and Kushta (roots of Saussurea lappa CB Clarke) in water.

nodes.label: Neem-Turmeric Decoction
nodes.Preparation: Crushed Neem leaves and Turmeric rhizome were boiled in water and filtered to obtain a herbal decoction

nodes.label: Babool bark decoction
nodes.Preparation: Fresh or dried Babool (Acacia arabica) bark was boiled in water until the volume was reduced, then filtered to obtain the decoction.

nodes.label: Lime Water
nodes.Preparation: Churnodaka (lime water) was prepared by mixing lime powder (calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂) with water, allowing it to stand for 12-24 hours and  filtering the clear supernatant.

nodes.label: Kushmanda Juice
nodes.Preparation: Fresh Kushmanda (ash gourd) pulp was crushed and manually squeezed to extract the juice, which was then filtered for use.

nodes.label: Eclipta Alba Juice
nodes.Preparation: Fresh Eclipta alba was washed, cut, blended for with distilled water, and the pulp was squeezed through cotton cloth to obtain fresh extract.

nodes.label: Jayanti Patra Swarasa
nodes.Preparation: Juice of Sesbania grandiflora leaves

nodes.label: Triphala Kwatha
nodes.Preparation: Triphala Kwatha is prepared by boiling equal parts of Emblica officinalis, Terminalia bellirica, and Terminalia chebula in water and reducing it to one-fourth, then filtering the decoction.

nodes.label: Sarjika Salila
nodes.Preparation: Sarjika Salila is prepared by dissolving Sarjika Kshara (alkaline sodium salt powder) in water and stirring well until a clear mildly alkaline solution is obtained.

nodes.label: Yavakshara
nodes.Preparation: Barley ash was dissolved in water, filtered and evaporated to obtain alkaline Yavakshara.

nodes.label: Guggulu Decoction
nodes.Preparation: Purified guggulu resin was dissolved in water, filtered and used as the liquid medium.

nodes.label: Horse Gram Decoction
nodes.Preparation: Coarsely powdered Dolichos biflorus (Horse gram) was boiled with water (generally 1:16 ratio) until reduced to one-fourth, then filtered to obtain Kulattha Kwatha.

nodes.label: Nirgundi -Turmeric Decoction
nodes.Preparation: Leaves of Vitex negundo (Nirgundi) and powder of Curcuma longa (turmeric) were boiled in water (typically 1:16 ratio) and reduced to one-fourth, then filtered to obtain the decoction.

nodes.label: Nirgundi Decoction
nodes.Preparation: Decoction prepared by boiling coarse powder or fresh leaves of Nirgundi (Vitex negundo) in water and reducing to one-fourth volume, then filtering for use as liquid medium.

nodes.label: Kanchanara Kwatha
nodes.Preparation: Decoction of Bauhinia variegata stem bark

nodes.label: Badari Kwatha
nodes.Preparation: Fresh or dried Badari (Ziziphus jujuba) fruits were boiled in water until the volume was reduced (typically to one-fourth), then filtered to obtain Badari Kwatha (decoction).

nodes.label: Gomutra Triphala Kashaya
nodes.Preparation: Gomutra Triphala Kashaya is an Ayurvedic decoction made by boiling Triphala (Haritaki, Bibhitaki, Amalaki) in cow urine until reduced to the desired volume and then filtering for use.

nodes.label: Suveeraka
nodes.Preparation: Suveeraka is a fermented sour liquid prepared by fermenting cereal flour (commonly barley or wheat) with water until it becomes acidic, then filtering before use.

Vishesha Shodhana
nodes.description: Vishesh Shodhana (Specific purification) is the drug-specific purification performed after Samanya Shodhana. It uses special media and procedures tailored to a particular substance to eliminate its unique toxic components and enhance its therapeutic safety and efficacy.

nodes.label: Samanya Shodhana
nodes.description: Samanya Shodhana (General purification) is the preliminary, common purification step applied to many metals, minerals, and toxic herbs using standard media such as water, cow urine, milk, oil, or herbal decoctions. Its purpose is to remove visible impurities, reduce basic toxicity, and make the material softer and suitable for further processing.

nodes.label: Eczema
nodes.description: Eczema is a skin disorder characterized by Itching erythema, Scaling, Edema, vesiculation, and Discharge

nodes.label: Marana
nodes.Process_Description: Marana is the calcination of purified metals and minerals through repeated cycles of grinding with herbal media and controlled heating (Puta). This converts the material into fine, ash-like Bhasma that is non-toxic, stable, and bioavailable.

nodes.label: Bhavana
nodes.Process_Description: Bhavana is wet grinding of powdered drugs with herbal juices or decoctions until the liquid is fully absorbed. This enhances detoxification, potency, and homogeneity.

nodes.label: Dhanyabhraka
nodes.Process_Description: Dhanyabhraka is a special purification method for mica in which powdered mica is mixed with rice grains, tied in cloth, and soaked or rubbed in water. The fine mica particles pass through the cloth while heavier impurities remain behind.

nodes.label: Bhanupaka
nodes.Process_Description: Bhanupaka involves triturating the drug with liquid media and exposing it to sunlight. The mild heat and UV exposure promote slow drying and gentle chemical transformation.

nodes.label: Jarana
nodes.Process_Description: Jarana is roasting metals or minerals with herbal powders or other additives until they become brittle and powdery. It reduces hardness and prepares the substance for incineration (Marana).

nodes.label: Amritikarana
nodes.Process_Description: Amritikarana is a post-processing step applied to prepared Bhasma using ghee or herbal substances and mild heating. It is done to remove any residual toxicity, improve safety, and enhance therapeutic potency.
